html:
The Central Pomo are a Pomo people of the Russian River valley around Hopland and of the coast near Point Arena, in northern California. Their language, now extinct, was one of seven Pomoan languages. All Pomo together may have numbered about 8,000 before contact.

They gathered acorns and seeds, fished, and are famous, like other Pomo, for very fine basketry, some decorated with feathers and shell beads. Russians at Fort Ross to the south traded in the region from 1812. Mexican and then American ranchers took the valley, and the Gold Rush brought violence. Neighbours: Northern Pomo and Kashaya.
